And the vizier likewise remained for two days in a boat, cast upon the planks, without food.
And in the desert also the waters prevailed,
and drowned many of the Ma'addites.
It is related
that a certain Bedouin, when the waters came,
mounted his wife upon one horse,
and his daughter upon another horse,
and he mounted another.
And the waters reached and overtook the two women, and they fell and were drowned;
while he ran toward a tree that was nearby and climbed it,
and abandoned the horse.
And he remained there for days until the waters abated.
Even lions and wild asses were seen upon the tops of the hills,
around which the water was surrounding them;
and being confounded, they did no harm to one another.
And in the year 467
[467] of the Arabs,
the Caliph al-Qa'im died of the disease of suffocation (angina) on the dawn of Thursday, the 13th
of Sha'ban,
being seventy-five years of age.
And he was of a yellowish complexion
from eating much tripe (or dry figs? {OCR?}).
And his grandson al-Muqtadi succeeded him.
For on that very night there was over him the danger of death,
according to the astrological judgment.
For Mars, the lord of Scorpio, his ascendant,
on that night descended into Gemini,
his house of death,
in diameter (opposition) to Saturn, which was in Sagittarius.
And both of them formed a quartile aspect with the zodiac sign of Pisces,
which was the sign of the horoscope of that full year.
After al-Qa'im, his grandson al-Muqtadi [ruled] nineteen years and five months.
And in the year 468
[468], the Arabs took Hisn Hadath of Mabbug from the Romans,
and after eight years during which the Romans were in it,
most of them being besieged by the Arabs.
And in that year there was a great war in Syria between the forces of the Turcomans and those of the Egyptians.
And famine and pestilence also followed the war,
especially in Damascus.
For almost all of its inhabitants perished,
and three thousand souls remained in it,
after there had been three hundred thousand in it;
and only two bakers,
after two hundred and forty.
And a house that had been bought for three thousand dinars
was sold for one dinar,
and there was no one who would buy [it].
And when there was a little abundance,
mice increased upon the people, on account of the lack of cats, which had already been eaten.
